in_text_mentions: A follow-up CT angiogram was done, which demonstrated marked stenosis of the left pulmonary artery along with an abnormal division of the right main pulmonary artery before the level of the hilum, as shown in Figure 4. Since no other syndromic features were evident, a provisional diagnosis was based solely on imaging.

In our patient, the inverted "V" sign can be appreciated clearly in Figure 4, supporting the suspicion for ATS based on imaging findings. However, this radiologic pattern is not pathognomonic and may also be seen in other heritable connective tissue disorders. Recognition of such imaging features is therefore important to prompt comprehensive cardiovascular evaluation and confirmatory genetic testing.

panels.rationale: This is a real-patient pulmonary artery angiogram from an article specifically about arterial tortuosity syndrome. The caption and in-text description directly identify tortuosity of the right pulmonary artery and multiple peripheral stenoses, both characteristic manifestations of the configured disease.

in_text_mentions: In view of these findings, cardiac catheterization was performed to confirm the hemodynamic data and to delineate the pulmonary artery anatomy. Pressure and oxygen saturation data is given in Table 1. Angiography revealed tortuous pulmonary arteries with multiple areas of peripheral stenoses [Figures 1 and 2]. The interventricular septum was intact. The aortic root and arch appeared elongated [Figure 3]. There was no arterial duct but the subclavian artery also showed a tortuous course. As no suitable therapeutic option could be offered, the patient was discharged on medical follow-up.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Axial CT showing pulmonary artery elongation, V-shaped early branching configuration, and segmental narrowing/dilations in a neonatal case of arterial tortuosity syndrome. b: Volume-rendered CT demonstrating the elongated, tortuous, and V-shaped configuration of the pulmonary arteries characteristic of arterial tortuosity syndrome.

panels.figure_caption: V sign of the pulmonary artery. ( a ) Axial contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) images with maximum intensity projection (MIP) reconstruction and ( b ) volume-rendered image showing elongation and early branching of pulmonary artery with a V -shaped configuration and winding course and segmenting narrowing and dilations ( black arrows ).
in_text_mentions: The main pulmonary artery appeared to be of a regular caliber ( Z -score: + 0,95) with early bifurcation (inverted V -shaped configuration at the axial CT scan) and relative elongation and narrowing of the right and left pulmonary arteries. The left pulmonary artery presented mid-distal narrowing followed by ectasia of the branch itself, which hyper-arborized the distal circles of both the pulmonary arterial districts (in the subhilar site; Fig. 6 ).
